## Pick C—but as the revision base, not a finished match

**C’s continuous coachwork is the strongest construction.** Its shoulder-to-front-fender transition reads more coherently, and the wheel openings look better integrated into the body. A reads as separate fender pieces; B retains a slab-sided, extruded appearance. C still shares substantial silhouette errors with both.

Using the supplied collage—not the older rounded prototype—as the shape reference:

| Area | Visible mismatch → actionable correction |
|---|---|
| **Proportion** | The models read as tall, short-cabin coupes with undersized wheels. The reference reads lower, wider and more stretched between large wheels. **Resolve wheel diameter, wheelbase and body height together in profile before detailing.** Avoid simply flattening the entire mesh. |
| **Glazing** | All three have a pronounced domed canopy and a relatively blunt rear termination. The reference’s glass forms a shallower, longer wedge with strongly tapered side glazing. **Lower the roof crown, refine windshield rake and extend the rearward glass taper.** |
| **Shoulders** | C improves continuity, but its upper body still looks inflated around the cabin. The reference combines a broad, flatter hood with distinct rising outer fender shoulders. **Keep the smooth fender blend while sharpening the hood/shoulder hierarchy; don’t turn the whole nose into one rounded surface.** |
| **Wheel arches** | C is preferable, but the small wheels and surrounding body mass weaken the open-arch effect. **Increase the wheels’ visual dominance, refine arch clearance and give the openings convincing inner depth.** These renders cannot establish actual topology or clearance throughout the opening. |
| **Front lamps** | The models’ dark, near-vertical corner recesses dominate the face. The reference shows compact, pale, angular lamp elements tucked into the hood/fender junction. **Reduce the black sockets and reshape/reposition the lamps around that junction**, preserving the broad, low nose and dark lower intake. |
| **Rear machinery** | The sheet reads as a shallow row of shiny mechanical circles. The reference has a **recessed, layered assembly**: upper circular outlets, darker machinery below, and separate outboard downward-facing nozzles. **Build depth, framing and component hierarchy before adding small detail.** The rear also needs a clearer upper-deck/spoiler relationship. |

**Revision order:** proportion → canopy/glazing → shoulder and arch sections → lamps → rear machinery.

Preserve the **silver planes, black glazing and ink-like outlines**; borrow shape from the photos, not their photographic finish. The reported verifier passes and ~50k triangles do not establish visual fidelity. Photo-based dimensional judgments here are inferred, not measured. No generation or graph changes made.
